q: How much CO2 does kaolin (china clay) processing emit per tonne?
title: Kaolin processing CO2 per tonne
short: Washed kaolin goes through slurrying, settling, filter pressing and drying. Drying fuel usually dominates, followed by pumping electricity. Calcined kaolin adds a kiln step that burns far more fuel per tonne, so report the two grades separately.
audience: China clay processors supplying ceramics, paper and paint

ul: Dryer and kiln fuel by grade.
Electricity for blungers, pumps and filter presses.
Tonnes dispatched by grade, dry basis.

p: Calcining drives off water bound in the clay; it is fuel heavy but not a carbonate, so there is no process CO2 like limestone.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
